general_information.Syllabus Name: Python for Applied Data Science _Lập trình Python cho khoa học dữ liệu ứng dụng
general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours + 1h FE + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: This hands-on course introduces students to Python programming with a specific focus on data science applications. Designed for beginners, it starts with the essentials of programming and guides learners through structured modules including Python basics, data structures, programming fundamentals, data handling, and APIs. Students will learn to write clean and efficient Python code, manipulate and analyze datasets, and automate data collection from external sources. Each topic is reinforced with review sessions and lab-based activities to ensure practical understanding and application. By the end of the course, students will be able to develop Python programs that solve real-world data problems and form a strong foundation for further study in data science and machine learning.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Student must complete the coursera course:https://www.coursera.org/learn/python-for-applied-data-science-ai/ - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU LMS at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information - Learn by coding practice
general_information.Tools: Anacoda, Jupyter Notebook, Google Colab, Visual Studio Code

description: This hands-on course introduces students to Python programming with a specific focus on data science applications. Designed for beginners, it starts with the essentials of programming and guides learners through structured modules including Python basics, data structures, programming fundamentals, data handling, and APIs. Students will learn to write clean and efficient Python code, manipulate and analyze datasets, and automate data collection from external sources. Each topic is reinforced with review sessions and lab-based activities to ensure practical understanding and application. By the end of the course, students will be able to develop Python programs that solve real-world data problems and form a strong foundation for further study in data science and machine learning.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Develop a foundational understanding of Python programming by learning basic syntax, data types, expressions, variables, and string operations.
Understand the key data structure in Python such as using data structures, conditions and branching, loops, functions, exception handling, objects, and classes.
Know how to apply proficiency in using Python libraries such as Pandas and Numpy and developing code using Jupyter Notebooks.
Understand and implement the way to access and extract web-based data by working with REST APIs using requests and performing web scraping
Apply AI tools to enhance Python programming skills and critically justify the logic of the implemented code

assessments.Question Type: Homework, mini-projects, and optionally the constructivist approach as proposed by the lecturer.
assessments.Grading Guide: Individual or team work, guided by instructor, submission by a given deadline
assessments.Note: Instructor has responsible for guiding students in carrying out the task View assignment on slot 20

assessments.Note: Instructor has resposibility to guide and review the lab practice for students.

assessments.Grading Guide: The examination is conducted by the exam board. A minimum of two teachers is required for grading the Final Project. Each team is allocated 30 minutes for the presentation of their project followed by a Q&A session. Evaluation of the final presentation is based on the final report, project demonstration, and Q&A interaction. The grade is determined by averaging the grades given by the two teachers.

assessments.Note: The exam questions must be updated or different at least 70% to the previous ones.
